docs.title: Welcome to xcorecli
docs.text:
xcorecli is the official command-line companion for the xcore ecosystem. It provides a unified interface for project management, service monitoring, plugin lifecycles, and worker orchestration.

Beautiful Terminal Output

xcorecli leverages the rich library to deliver stunning terminal interfaces, featuring interactive tables, progress bars, and real-time dashboards.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Project Initialization: Seamlessly scaffold new projects and manage integration.yaml.
  • Plugin Lifecycle: Full control over installing, signing, and updating plugins.
  • Real-time Monitoring: Integrated dashboard for service health and resource usage.
  • Worker Orchestration: Manage Celery/XWorker processes with ease.
  • Security & Sandboxing: Resource isolation and AST-based whitelisting for plugins.
  • Database Migrations: Streamlined Alembic integration for schema management.

docs.title: Quick Start Overview
docs.text:
Quick Install
git clone https://github.com/your-repo/xcorecli.git
cd xcorecli
make install

Architecture

The CLI is designed to be highly modular. Each command group (e.g., plugin, worker, manager) is a self-contained module, ensuring extensibility and maintainability.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: A comprehensive list of all commands available in xcorecli.

docs.title: Global Commands
docs.text:
• xcli init: Initialize a new xcore project.
  • xcli upgrade: Migrate integration.yaml to the latest schema.
  • xcli health: Global health check of all configured services.
  • xcli services: Show status and details of all system services.

docs.title: manager Administration
docs.text:
• manager start: Start the FastAPI server (uvicorn).
  • manager stop: Stop the detached API server.
  • manager top: Full-screen live dashboard (resources + logs).
  • manager logs: Stream and filter application logs.
  • manager resources: Live resource usage per plugin.
  • manager metrics: Application metrics snapshot.
  • manager services list: List all services.
  • manager services reload: Reconnect a service.
  • manager services unload: Shutdown a service.

docs.title: plugin Lifecycle
docs.text:
• plugin info: Detailed local plugin report.
  • plugin health: Health check of all installed plugins.
  • plugin remove: Uninstall a plugin.
  • plugin install: Install from marketplace/git/zip.
  • plugin versions: List marketplace versions.

docs.title: plugin local Development
docs.text:
• local scaffold: Create a new plugin from template.
  • local link: Symlink a local directory.
  • local unlink: Remove a symlink.
  • local list: List all plugins with link type.

docs.title: plugin marketplace Discovery
docs.text:
• marketplace browse: List all available plugins.
  • marketplace search: Search by keyword.
  • marketplace info: Pre-install details.
  • marketplace trending: Show popular plugins.
  • marketplace rate: Rate 15 stars.

docs.title: plugin update Maintenance
docs.text:
• update check: Check for new versions.
  • update apply: Apply updates (--all, --dry-run).

docs.title: plugin runtime Control
docs.text:
• runtime load: Activate a plugin.
  • runtime unload: Deactivate a plugin.
  • runtime reload: Restart a plugin.
  • runtime status: Show active plugins.

docs.title: worker Background Tasks
docs.text:
• worker start: Start a Celery worker.
  • worker beat: Start the scheduler.
  • worker inspect: List tasks and nodes.
  • worker purge: Clear a task queue.

docs.title: worker process Orchestration
docs.text:
• process start: Start multiple instances.
  • process stop: Shutdown all workers.
  • process restart: Restart all workers.
  • process status: Table of running worker PIDs.
  • process logs: Tail worker-specific logs.

docs.title: migration Database
docs.text:
• migration init: Setup Alembic.
  • migration scan: Preview discovered models.
  • migration backup: Create a DB backup.
  • migration restore: Restore from backup.
  • migration backups: List available backups.
  • migration revision: Create a new migration.
  • migration upgrade: Apply migrations (--backup).
  • migration downgrade: Rollback migrations.
  • migration history: Show migration list.

docs.title: Health & Services
docs.text: Monitoring the status of your xcore ecosystem is vital for maintaining a healthy production environment.

docs.title: Global Health Check
docs.text:
The health command performs an exhaustive check of all configured services and components.

Check Everything
xcli health

This command validates: - Connectivity: Database and Redis connections. - Plugins: Integrity and loading status. - Worker: Celery/XWorker availability. - Environment: Python version and required dependencies.

Service Failures

If any critical service is down, xcli health will return a non-zero exit code, making it suitable for CI/CD health gates.

docs.title: Service Status
docs.text:
For a more focused view of system services, use the services command.

Service Overview
xcli services

docs.title: Features:
docs.text:
• Real-time Status: Shows which services are UP, DOWN, or DEGRADED.
  • Resource Usage: Brief overview of memory/CPU used by each service.
  • Rich Table: Displays information in a beautiful, easy-to-read table format.

Service Management

Individual services can be managed via the manager services command group. See Service Management for more details.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If health reports errors: 1. Check the logs: make logs 2. Validate configuration: xcli config validate 3. Restart services: make restart

docs.title: Project Initialization
docs.text: xcorecli simplifies the lifecycle of an xcore project from scaffolding to upgrades.

docs.title: New Project Scaffolding
docs.text:
To start a new project, use the init command. The improved wizard will guide you through the setup, providing sensible defaults for various database engines.

Interactive Init
xcli init my-project

docs.title: Database Options
docs.text: The initialization wizard supports several database backends with pre-configured URL templates: - SQLite: sqlite:///./data/xcore.db (Default) - PostgreSQL: postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db - MySQL: mysql+pymysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/db - MariaDB: mysql+pymysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/db

docs.title: Generated Structure
docs.text:
xcli init generates a complete, production-ready project structure:

  • integration.yaml: Central configuration file.
  • main.py: Application entry point with a built-in health check endpoint and plugin loading logic.
  • .env: Environment variables for sensitive configuration (DB passwords, API keys).
  • requirements.txt: Project dependencies.
  • plugins/: Directory for your custom extensions.
  • log/: Directory for application logs.

Built-in Health Check

The generated main.py includes a /health endpoint by default, allowing you to monitor the status of all connected services (DB, Cache, etc.) via HTTP.

docs.title: Upgrade Workflows
docs.text: As the xcore ecosystem evolves, your project may need updates to its core configuration or database schema.

docs.title: Upgrading Configuration
docs.text:
The upgrade command checks your current integration.yaml against the latest schema and suggests migrations or additions.

xcli upgrade

Automation

Running make init (if using the provided Makefile) is the recommended way to handle both installation and initial configuration in one go.

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
1. Scaffold: xcli init my-project --db postgresql
  2. Install: pip install -r requirements.txt
  3. Run: xcli manager start --reload
  4. Verify: Open http://localhost:8000/health

docs.title: CLI Configuration
docs.text: The config command group allows you to manage the behavior of xcorecli itself and its interaction with the xcore project.

docs.title: Commands Overview
docs.text: Command Description show Display the current merged configuration. get Retrieve a specific configuration value. set Update a configuration value. validate Check integration.yaml for schema compliance.

docs.title: Viewing Configuration
docs.text:
To see your current setup, including defaults and overrides from integration.yaml:

xcli config show

docs.title: Updating Values
docs.text:
You can modify settings directly from the CLI. These changes are typically applied to your local configuration or the project's integration.yaml.

Set Value
xcli config set app.debug true

Layered Configuration

xcorecli uses a layered approach: 1. Internal Defaults 2. integration.yaml (Project level) 3. Local CLI Config (User level) 4. Environment Variables

docs.title: Runtime Configuration
docs.text:
Some settings in the runtime section of integration.yaml can be adjusted without restarting the entire system, such as plugin reload intervals.

plugins:
  interval: 5 # Check for changes every 5 seconds

Dynamic Updates

Use xcli manager services reload to apply certain configuration changes on the fly.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: To interact with the xcore marketplace and perform secure operations, you need to configure your credentials.

docs.title: Configuration Commands
docs.text: xcorecli provides a config command group to manage your local settings.

docs.title: Set Authentication Token
docs.text:
Use the set command to store your marketplace API key:

Configuration
xcli config set marketplace.api_key "your-secure-token"

Security First

Never share your API keys or commit them to version control. xcorecli stores these credentials securely in your local environment.

docs.title: View Current Configuration
docs.text:
To check your current configuration (with sensitive data masked):

xcli config show

docs.title: Credential Storage
docs.text:
Credentials and sensitive settings are managed by the xcli/_credentials.py module, which ensures that: - API keys are handled securely. - Tokens are used for marketplace interactions (marketplace.xcorehub.dev).

Marketplace Integration

By default, xcorecli connects to https://marketplace.xcorehub.dev. You can override this URL in your integration.yaml or via the config command.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Alternatively, you can use environment variables for CI/CD environments:

.env
XCORE_MARKETPLACE_API_KEY=your-token

docs.title: Configuration Guide
docs.text: The heart of any xcore project is the integration.yaml file. This central configuration file defines how services, plugins, and the core system behave.

docs.title: The Role of integration.yaml
docs.text:
integration.yaml acts as the "Source of Truth" for your application. It controls:

  • App Metadata: Name, environment, and debug settings.
  • FastAPI/Uvicorn: Server host, port, and API documentation details.
  • Plugins: Directory location, security keys, and hot-reload intervals.
  • Services: Database connections (SQLAlchemy/Redis), caching, and task scheduling.
  • Worker: Celery/XWorker configurations including brokers and queues.
  • Observability: Logging levels, Prometheus metrics, and tracing.
  • Security: AST-based whitelists for plugin sandboxing.

docs.title: Basic Structure
docs.text:
integration.yaml
app:
  name: my-xcore-app
  env: development
  debug: true

plugins:
  directory: ./plugins
  strict_trusted: true
  interval: 10

services:
  databases:
    db:
      type: sqlasync
      url: sqlite+aiosqlite:///db.sqlite3

docs.title: Security & Sandboxing
docs.text:
The security section defines which Python modules are allowed within the plugin sandbox.

security:
  allowed_imports:
    - fastapi
    - json
    - datetime
  forbidden_imports:
    - os

docs.title: Plugin Management
docs.text:
Configure how plugins are loaded and verified.

Plugin Verification

plugins.secret_key is used to verify HMAC-SHA256 signatures (plugin.sig) of your plugins.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
Manage logs and metrics from one place.

observability:
  logging:
    level: INFO
    file: log/app.log

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: xcorecli validates this file upon startup to ensure all required fields are present and correctly typed. Use xcli config validate to check your configuration manually.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Getting started with xcorecli is straightforward. The project uses Poetry for dependency management and a Makefile to automate common tasks.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python: 3.12 or higher.
  • Poetry: Recommended for environment management.
  • Make: To use the provided automation scripts.

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/your-repo/xcorecli.git
cd xcorecli

docs.title: 2. Install Dependencies
docs.text:
You can use the provided Makefile to set up the environment and install all necessary packages.

Standard Installation
make install

What happens under the hood?

make install runs poetry lock and poetry install, creating a virtual environment and installing all project dependencies listed in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: 3. Initialize the Project
docs.text:
After installation, initialize the environment:

Initialization
make init

This script sets up necessary permissions and starts the development environment.

docs.title: Development Environment
docs.text:
For contributors, you can install additional development and documentation tools:

Dev Setup
make auto-setup

MkDocs Serve

To view this documentation locally with live-reload, run: 

make docs-serve

docs.title: Python Environment Detection
docs.text:
If you need to check which Python environment xcorecli is using:

make autobuild-ast

docs.title: Administration Dashboard
docs.text: The manager command group is your high-level control center for the entire xcore project. It provides a suite of tools for monitoring, service management, and system-wide administration.

docs.title: The Manager Concept
docs.text: While other commands focus on specific components (like plugin or worker), the manager provides an aggregated view and orchestration capabilities for the whole system.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
• Server Management: Start and stop the FastAPI/Uvicorn server.
  • Real-time Monitoring: Full-screen "top-like" dashboard.
  • Resource Analytics: Detailed memory and CPU profiling per plugin.
  • Service Orchestration: Hot-reloading and unloading of system services.
  • Log Aggregation: Unified view of logs from multiple sources.

docs.title: Server Management
docs.text: You can manage your API server directly from the CLI.

docs.title: Start the Server
docs.text:
Development mode
xcli manager start --reload
Production mode
xcli manager start --workers 4 --detach

docs.title: Stop the Server
docs.text:
If started with --detach, you can stop it using:

xcli manager stop

docs.title: The top Dashboard
docs.text:
To launch the main management interface:

xcli manager top

docs.title: Service Management
docs.text:
The services sub-app allows fine-grained control over individual providers (DB, Cache, etc.).

xcli manager services list
xcli manager services reload db

docs.title: In this section:
docs.text:
• Real-time Monitoring
  • Service Management

docs.title: Real-time Monitoring
docs.text: xcorecli provides powerful monitoring tools to help you keep an eye on your system's performance and health.

docs.title: The top Dashboard
docs.text:
The flagship monitoring tool is xcli manager top. It provides a comprehensive, real-time dashboard inside your terminal.

Launch Dashboard
xcli manager top

docs.title: Dashboard Tabs:
docs.text:
1. System: CPU, Memory, Disk, and Network usage.
  2. Services: Status and uptime of databases, cache, and API.
  3. Workers: Active Celery tasks and worker health.
  4. Plugins: Resource usage per plugin.

docs.title: Resource Profiling
docs.text:
For a more data-focused view of resource consumption:

Resource Summary
xcli manager resources

This command generates a detailed report of which components are consuming the most memory and CPU cycles. Use the --watch flag for a live-updating table.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
If metrics are enabled in integration.yaml, you can view a snapshot of counters and gauges:

xcli manager metrics

docs.title: Unified Logs
docs.text:
Instead of tailing multiple files, use the manager's log viewer to see a merged stream of application, worker, and plugin logs.

Follow Logs
xcli manager logs --follow

Filtering Logs

You can filter logs by a specific plugin name to reduce noise: 

xcli manager logs my-plugin --follow

Configuration

Observability settings are defined in the observability section of your integration.yaml. 

observability:
  logging:
    file: "log/xcore.log"

docs.title: Service Management
docs.text: Control the lifecycle of individual system services (Databases, Cache, Extensions) without affecting the rest of the application.

docs.title: Service Operations
docs.text: The manager services command group allows you to manage services defined in the services section of integration.yaml.

docs.title: List Services
docs.text:
See all configured services, their initialization status, and current health.

xcli manager services list

Live View

Use the --watch (or -w) flag to keep the table updated in real-time. 

xcli manager services list --watch

docs.title: Reload a Service
docs.text:
Force a service to re-read its configuration and reconnect. Useful for rotating database credentials or updating API keys.

xcli manager services reload db

docs.title: Unload/Disable a Service
docs.text:
Temporarily disable a service and shut down its connections.

xcli manager services unload cache

Dependencies

Be careful when unloading core services like db or redis_db, as most plugins and internal components depend on them.

docs.title: Dynamic Extensions
docs.text:
Services defined under services.extensions can often be hot-swapped or reloaded on the fly.

services:
  extensions:
    email:
      module: extensions.email.service:EmailService

You can reload this extension using: 

xcli manager services reload email

Service Container

All services are managed by a central ServiceContainer. The manager commands interact with this container to ensure thread-safe operations.

docs.title: Database Migrations
docs.text: xcorecli provides a streamlined wrapper around Alembic to manage your database schema migrations, with added safety features like automated backups.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Migrations are managed via the migration command group.

docs.title: Initialize Migrations
docs.text:
If you are setting up a new project:

xcli migration init

This creates the alembic/ directory, configuration files, and scans for initial models.

docs.title: Safety & Backups
docs.text: Before performing dangerous operations, xcorecli can automatically backup your database.

docs.title: Create a Backup
docs.text:
Manually trigger a timestamped backup. Supports SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB.

xcli migration backup

docs.title: Restore from Backup
docs.text:
Restore your database to a previous state. If no path is provided, it picks the latest backup.

xcli migration restore

docs.title: Manage Backups
docs.text:
List all available backups and their sizes.

xcli migration backups

Backup Storage

Backups are stored in the directory specified in integration.yaml under migration.backup_dir (defaults to ./backups).

docs.title: Scan for Models
docs.text:
Preview all discovered SQLAlchemy models across your project and plugins before generating a migration.

xcli migration scan

Scan Paths

xcorecli supports multiple scan paths in integration.yaml. By default, it scans your main app and all installed plugins.

docs.title: Create a New Migration
docs.text:
Generate a new migration script based on changes to your models.

Generate Migration
xcli migration revision -m "add user table"

docs.title: Apply Migrations
docs.text:
Upgrade your database to the latest schema version.

Upgrade with Backup
xcli migration upgrade head --backup

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Revert the last migration.

Downgrade
xcli migration downgrade -1

docs.title: Migration Status
docs.text:
Check which migrations have been applied.

xcli migration history

Stamping

Use xcli migration stamp <id> to mark the database at a specific revision without running the actual migration scripts.

docs.title: Plugin System
docs.text: The xcore framework is designed around a powerful, modular plugin system. Plugins allow you to extend the core functionality of your application without modifying the kernel.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Plugins in xcore are self-contained modules located in the directory specified in integration.yaml (usually ./plugins/).

docs.title: Types of Plugins
docs.text:
1. Trusted Plugins:
  2. Have full access to the system.
  3. Typically developed internally.

  4. Must be signed if strict_trusted is enabled.

  5. Sandboxed Plugins:

  6. Run in an isolated environment.
  7. Restricted by an AST-based whitelist for imports.
  8. Limited resource consumption (CPU, Memory, Disk).

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
A typical plugin looks like this:

plugins/
└── my-plugin/
    ├── src/
    │   └── main.py      # Entry point
    ├── plugin.yaml      # Metadata & Resources
    ├── plugin.sig       # Security signature
    └── requirements.txt # Dependencies

docs.title: Lifecycle Management
docs.text:
xcorecli provides a comprehensive suite of commands to manage the entire plugin lifecycle:

  • Development: Local Linking & Scaffolding
  • Deployment: Installation & Removal
  • Runtime: Load/Unload/Reload
  • Discovery: Marketplace
  • Security: Signing & Health Checks
  • Maintenance: Updates

docs.title: Top-level Commands
docs.text:
In addition to sub-apps, the plugin group provides several direct commands:

  • xcli plugin info <name>: Show detailed manifest and permissions for an installed plugin.
  • xcli plugin health: Perform a global health check (signatures, AST, manifests) on all installed plugins.
  • xcli plugin remove <name>: Uninstall a plugin and delete its files.

IPC (Inter-Plugin Communication)

Plugins can communicate with each other using the built-in IPC mechanism, which is enforced by the core ServiceContainer.

docs.title: Installing Plugins
docs.text: Plugins can be installed from the official xcore Marketplace or from external sources like Git repositories.

docs.title: Installing from Marketplace
docs.text:
The easiest way to add features. xcorecli handles downloads and HMAC signature verification.

Marketplace Install
xcli plugin install name-of-plugin

docs.title: Installing a Specific Version
docs.text:
xcli plugin install name-of-plugin@1.2.3

To see all available versions for a plugin: 

xcli plugin versions name-of-plugin

docs.title: Installing from Git or URL
docs.text:
You can install plugins directly from a Git repository or a hosted .zip file.

Git Install
xcli plugin install my-plugin --source git --url https://github.com/user/plugin.git

docs.title: Detailed Info
docs.text:
Get a full report on an installed plugin, including its author, description, requested permissions, and resource limits.

xcli plugin info name-of-plugin

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
Verify the integrity of all installed plugins. This checks if manifests are valid, signatures match, and if sandboxed plugins follow AST import rules.

xcli plugin health

docs.title: Removal
docs.text:
Uninstall a plugin and remove its directory.

xcli plugin remove name-of-plugin

Security

xcorecli verifies the HMAC signature of marketplace plugins. For Git or local installs, we recommend running xcli plugin health after installation.

docs.title: Local Plugin Development
docs.text: The plugin local command group is designed to accelerate the development of new features.

docs.title: Scaffolding a New Plugin
docs.text:
Create a new plugin structure with one command. The improved scaffold command supports several flags to pre-configure your code.

Rich Scaffolding
xcli plugin local scaffold my_plugin \
  --mode sandboxed \
  --db \
  --cache \
  --scheduler

docs.title: Scaffold Flags:
docs.text:
• --mode: trusted (default) or sandboxed.
  • --db: Generates models.py and schemas.py.
  • --cache: Injects the cache service into the plugin.
  • --scheduler: Injects the scheduler service.
  • --no-routes: Skips generating FastAPI router code.

docs.title: Linking for Development
docs.text:
Instead of installing a plugin, you can create a symbolic link from your development directory to the project's plugin folder. This allows you to see changes instantly.

Link Plugin
xcli plugin local link --path /path/to/your/source --name my-plugin

docs.title: Unlinking
docs.text:
When you're done developing or want to switch to a production version:

xcli plugin local unlink my-plugin

docs.title: Listing Plugins
docs.text:
The local list command shows all plugins and identifies whether they are installed (physical files) or symlinked (local development).

xcli plugin local list

Hot Reload

Ensure debug: true and a valid interval are set in your integration.yaml for the best development experience.

docs.title: Plugin Marketplace
docs.text: Discover and explore new capabilities for your xcore project via the official marketplace.

docs.title: Browse All
docs.text:
List everything available on the marketplace.

xcli plugin marketplace browse

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Find plugins by keywords, tags, or categories.

Search
xcli plugin marketplace search "monitoring"

docs.title: Trending
docs.text:
See what's popular in the community.

xcli plugin marketplace trending

docs.title: Viewing Plugin Details
docs.text:
Get in-depth information about a specific marketplace plugin before installing it.

Plugin Info
xcli plugin marketplace info name-of-plugin

docs.title: Rating Plugins
docs.text:
Share your experience by rating a plugin (1 to 5 stars).

xcli plugin marketplace rate name-of-plugin --score 5

API Keys

Interacting with the marketplace requires an API key. Configure it using xcli config set api-key xdk_....

docs.title: Runtime Management
docs.text: Manage the operational state of your plugins without restarting the entire application.

docs.title: Controlling Plugin State
docs.text: The plugin runtime command group provides direct control over the loading mechanism.

docs.title: Load a Plugin
docs.text:
If a plugin is installed but not active:

xcli plugin runtime load my-plugin

docs.title: Unload a Plugin
docs.text:
To temporarily disable a plugin and free up resources:

xcli plugin runtime unload my-plugin

docs.title: Reload a Plugin
docs.text:
Useful for applying updates or configuration changes:

xcli plugin runtime reload my-plugin

Hot Reloading

xcore supports automatic hot-reloading. Configure the interval in integration.yaml to enable it: 

plugins:
  interval: 10 # Check every 10 seconds

docs.title: Call a Plugin Action
docs.text:
You can trigger a specific action within a plugin directly from the CLI, passing a JSON payload if required.

xcli plugin runtime call my-plugin send_email --payload '{"to": "user@example.com", "subject": "Hello"}'

docs.title: Monitoring Runtime Status
docs.text:
To see which plugins are currently loaded and their operational state (e.g., running, initializing):

xcli plugin runtime status

docs.title: Global Reload
docs.text:
To reload all active plugins at once:

xcli plugin runtime reload-all

State Persistence

When a plugin is reloaded, its in-memory state is lost. Ensure your plugins implement proper state persistence (e.g., via the cache service) if needed.

docs.title: Plugin Security & Signing
docs.text: Security is a core pillar of the xcore plugin system. We provide tools to ensure that only verified and safe code runs in your environment.

docs.title: Signing Plugins
docs.text:
For production use, plugins should be signed to prevent tampering. Signing uses an HMAC-SHA256 hash based on the plugin's content and a secret key.

Sign Plugin
xcli plugin security sign my-plugin --key "your-secret-signing-key"

This creates a plugin.sig file within the plugin directory.

Secret Key Management

The plugins.secret_key in your integration.yaml must match the key used for signing for verification to succeed.

docs.title: Verification & Health
docs.text:
You can manually verify the integrity of a plugin:

xcli plugin security verify my-plugin

For a comprehensive check of all plugins (including manifest validation and AST analysis), use:

xcli plugin health

docs.title: Strict Mode
docs.text:
Enable strict_trusted in your configuration to refuse any plugin that is not properly signed.

plugins:
  strict_trusted: true

docs.title: AST Whitelisting
docs.text:
For Sandboxed Plugins, xcore uses an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analyzer to restrict imports.

  • Allowed: json, math, fastapi, etc.
  • Forbidden: os, subprocess, shutil, etc.

This prevents plugins from performing unauthorized filesystem or system operations.

Customizing Whitelists

Modify the security.allowed_imports section in integration.yaml to suit your project's needs.

docs.title: Managing Updates
docs.text: Keep your plugins up to date with the latest features and security patches.

docs.title: Checking for Updates
docs.text:
Check all installed plugins against the marketplace to see if newer versions are available.

Check Updates
xcli plugin update check

docs.title: Applying Updates
docs.text: The update apply command allows you to update a single plugin or your entire fleet.

docs.title: Update a Single Plugin
docs.text: xcli plugin update apply my-plugin

docs.title: Update All Plugins
docs.text: xcli plugin update apply --all

docs.title: Safe Updates (Dry Run)
docs.text:
See which plugins would be updated and to what versions without actually downloading anything.

xcli plugin update apply --all --dry-run

docs.title: Targeting a Version
docs.text:
xcli plugin update apply my-plugin --version 2.0.0

Breaking Changes

Always review the changelog on the marketplace before updating critical plugins. You can view the latest info using xcli plugin marketplace info.

docs.title: Plugin Sandboxing
docs.text: The Sandbox provides a secure execution environment for third-party or untrusted plugins, ensuring they cannot compromise the host system.

docs.title: Resource Isolation
docs.text: Sandboxed plugins are restricted in their resource consumption to prevent "noisy neighbor" issues or intentional Denial of Service.

docs.title: Limits Configuration
docs.text:
You can define default limits in integration.yaml:

security:
  rate_limit_default:
    calls: 200        # Max IPC calls
    period_seconds: 60 # Per minute

docs.title: AST-Based Whitelisting
docs.text:
The core of the sandbox is an AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) analyzer that scans the plugin's code before execution.

  • Whitelisted: Only modules listed in security.allowed_imports can be imported.
  • Blacklisted: Modules in security.forbidden_imports (like os or subprocess) are explicitly blocked.

Sandbox Bypass

Attempting to bypass the sandbox via reflection or other advanced Python techniques is monitored and will result in the plugin being immediately unloaded.

docs.title: Managing the Sandbox
docs.text:
Use the sandbox command group to inspect the status of the isolation layer.

# View sandbox statistics
xcli sandbox stats

# Inspect a specific plugin's sandbox
xcli sandbox inspect my-sandboxed-plugin

Trusted vs. Sandboxed

By default, plugins are treated as Sandboxed. You must explicitly mark a plugin as Trusted in its plugin.yaml (and usually sign it) to run it with full permissions.

docs.title: Worker Orchestration
docs.text: xcore integrates with Celery to handle background tasks, scheduled jobs, and asynchronous processing.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The worker command group allows you to manage the lifecycle of your background processing fleet.

docs.title: Key Commands
docs.text:
• start: Launch a Celery worker.
  • beat: Start the periodic task scheduler.
  • inspect: Check worker health and registered tasks.
  • purge: Clear all messages from a queue.
  • process: Fine-grained process management sub-app.

docs.title: Start a Worker
docs.text:
By default, worker start launches a Celery worker. API server management has moved to manager start.

Start Celery
xcli worker start

docs.title: Inspect Workers
docs.text:
Check which worker nodes are online and what tasks they are capable of running.

Inspect
xcli worker inspect

docs.title: Purging Queues
docs.text:
If you have a buildup of unwanted tasks, you can clear a queue:

xcli worker purge default

docs.title: Periodic Tasks (Beat)
docs.text:
To start the scheduler that triggers periodic tasks:

xcli worker beat

Configuration

Worker settings like broker_url, concurrency, and queues are managed in the services.xworker section of integration.yaml.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: For detailed control over multiple worker processes, including logs and status tables, see Process Management.

docs.title: Worker Process Management
docs.text: The worker process sub-app provides fine-grained control over multiple background worker instances.

docs.title: Start Multiple Instances
docs.text:
Start several worker instances at once, each with its own hostname.

xcli worker process start --count 4

docs.title: Advanced Start Flags
docs.text:
• --queues / -Q: Comma-separated list of queues to listen to.
  • --concurrency: Number of child processes per worker instance.
  • --detach / -d: Run workers in the background.
xcli worker process start --queues priority,emails --concurrency 8 --detach

docs.title: Stop
docs.text:
Gracefully shut down all running worker processes.

xcli worker process stop

docs.title: Restart
docs.text:
Stop then restart all worker processes to apply code changes.

xcli worker process restart

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
See a detailed table of running worker processes, including their PIDs, uptime, and resource usage.

Process Status
xcli worker process status

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Tail the logs specifically for the worker processes.

Worker Logs
xcli worker process logs --lines 50 --follow

Background Processes

Status and log commands are particularly useful when workers are started with the --detach flag.
